title: 19. En Chine, les familles remboursent leurs dettes
gist: Chinese households are paying down debt at the fastest pace in decades: their consumer loans, including mortgages, fell by 1.6 trillion yuan in the first nine months of the year. Economists say people are spending less and using the money to repay loans, because property prices are falling and jobs are hard to find. Beijing has not launched a big stimulus to boost spending.

body.fr: En Chine, les familles {{remboursent|pay back (from rembourser)}} leurs {{dettes|debts}}.

bd.meaning: In China, families are paying back their debts.
chunks: in China (en before a feminine country)
pay back — the -ent ending marks a plural subject
bd.key: The present covers “are doing”: remboursent = “pay back” or “are paying back.” French has no separate -ing form.

body.fr: C'est le {{rythme|pace, speed}} {{le plus rapide|the fastest}} {{depuis des dizaines d'années|in decades}}.

bd.meaning: It's the fastest pace in decades.
chunks: it is — the set phrase c'est
in decades (literally: since tens of years)
bd.key: le plus + adjective = “the most ___ / the ___-est.” le plus rapide = “the fastest,” and it comes after the noun.

body.fr: {{Entre janvier et septembre|between January and September}}, leurs {{prêts|loans}} {{ont baissé|went down}} de 1 600 {{milliards|billions}} de yuans.

bd.meaning: Between January and September, their loans fell by 1.6 trillion yuan.
chunks: between January and September (months take no capital letter)
their loans — this total includes home loans
bd.key: milliard = billion. Careful: the French word billion means a trillion, so news writes big sums in milliards.

body.fr: {{L'année dernière|last year}}, ils ont baissé de 500 milliards de yuans {{sur toute l'année|over the whole year}}.

bd.meaning: Last year, they fell by 500 billion yuan over the whole year.
chunks: last year (dernière comes after the noun)
they went down ('ils' = the loans, masculine)
bd.key: Past = avoir + past form: ont baissé = “went down.” Only ont changes with the subject.

body.fr: Les {{statistiques|statistics, records}} {{commencent|start}} en 2005.

bd.meaning: The records start in 2005.
bd.key: “en” before a year = “in”: en 2005, en 2025.

body.fr: {{C'était|it was}} la {{première baisse|first drop}}.

bd.meaning: It was the first drop.
chunks: it was — the past of c'est
the first drop (baisse = a fall, from baisser)
bd.key: c'est → c'était: “it is” becomes “it was.” The -ait ending is the past used for describing.

body.fr: {{Depuis des années|for years}}, le {{marché immobilier|housing market}} {{va mal|is doing badly}}.

bd.meaning: For years, the housing market has been doing badly.
chunks: the housing / property market ('immobilier' after the noun)
is doing badly (aller mal = to be in a bad way)
bd.key: depuis + present = “has been … for”: French keeps the verb in the present (va mal) because it's still going on.

body.fr: Les familles remboursent donc leurs {{prêts immobiliers|mortgages (home loans)}}.

bd.meaning: So families are paying back their mortgages.
chunks: so / therefore — it sits after the verb here
bd.key: Adjective after the noun, and agreeing: prêts immobiliers — plural noun, so the adjective takes an -s too.

body.fr: Maintenant, les {{autres|other}} dettes baissent aussi, {{comme|like}} les {{cartes de crédit|credit cards}} et les prêts pour les voitures.

bd.meaning: Now other debts are falling too, like credit cards and car loans.
chunks: et les prêts pour les voitures
and car loans (literally: loans for cars)
bd.key: French builds compound nouns with “de / pour”: cartes de crédit, prêts pour les voitures — English just stacks the words (“car loans”).

body.fr: Robin Xing est {{économiste|economist}} {{chez|at (a company)}} Morgan Stanley, une grande banque.

bd.meaning: Robin Xing is an economist at Morgan Stanley, a big bank.
chunks: Robin Xing is an economist — no 'un' before a job
at Morgan Stanley (chez = at someone's place / company)
a big bank ('grande' before the noun)
bd.key: No “a” before a job after être: il est économiste = “he is an economist.”

body.fr: {{Selon lui|according to him}}, les gens {{dépensent moins|spend less}} et utilisent leur argent pour rembourser leurs dettes.

bd.meaning: According to him, people are spending less and using their money to pay back their debts.
chunks: and use their money (leur = their, one thing)
bd.key: pour + plain verb = “in order to”: pour rembourser — the verb after pour stays plain.

body.fr: Il dit que, dans la Chine {{moderne|modern}}, la dette {{n'a jamais baissé|has never fallen}} {{si vite|so fast}}.

bd.meaning: He says that in modern China, debt has never fallen so fast.
chunks: has never gone down — ne…jamais wraps the helper 'a'
bd.key: ne … jamais = “never”: same sandwich as ne … pas. In the past it wraps the helper: n'a jamais baissé.

body.fr: Dans les {{magasins|shops}}, les {{ventes|sales}} {{augmentent très peu|are barely growing}}.

bd.meaning: In shops, sales are barely growing.
bd.key: très peu = “very little”: it sits right after the verb (augmentent très peu).

body.fr: En octobre, elles ont augmenté de {{seulement|only}} 0,4 %.

bd.meaning: In October, they went up by only 0.4%.
chunks: they went up ('elles' = les ventes, feminine)
by only 0.4% — French uses a comma for the decimal point
bd.key: Decimal comma: 0,4 % = 0.4%. French also puts a space before the % sign.

body.fr: En 2025, c'était 3,8 % {{en moyenne|on average}}.

bd.meaning: In 2025, it was 3.8% on average.
bd.key: c'était again: the past of c'est, for describing how things were.

body.fr: Une {{autre|other}} économiste, Sheana Yue, {{explique pourquoi|explains why}}.

bd.meaning: Another economist, Sheana Yue, explains why.
chunks: another (female) economist — 'une' tells you she's a woman
bd.key: The little word shows gender: économiste is the same word for men and women; une tells you it's a woman.

body.fr: Les maisons {{perdent de la valeur|lose value}}, donc les familles sont {{moins riches|less rich}}.

bd.meaning: Homes are losing value, so families are less wealthy.
bd.key: moins + adjective = “less ___”: moins riches = “less rich / poorer.”

body.fr: Elles {{ne savent pas|don't know}} {{ce qui va arriver|what is going to happen}} aux prix.

bd.meaning: They don't know what's going to happen to prices.
chunks: what (as the subject of the next verb)
is going to happen (aller + plain verb)
bd.key: aller + plain verb = near future: va arriver = “is going to happen.” Only va changes.

body.fr: {{Alors|so}} elles remboursent leurs dettes et {{attendent pour acheter|wait before buying}}.

bd.meaning: So they pay back their debts and hold off on buying.
bd.key: One subject, two verbs: elles remboursent … et attendent — both take the plural -ent, no need to repeat elles.

body.fr: En 2026, le {{gouvernement|government}} chinois {{n'a pas lancé|has not launched}} de grand {{plan de relance|stimulus plan}}.

bd.meaning: In 2026, the Chinese government has not launched a big stimulus plan.
chunks: the Chinese government ('chinois' after the noun, no capital)
has not launched — ne…pas around the helper 'a'
a big stimulus plan (un → de after a negative; relance = a boost, restart)
bd.key: After a negative, un/une → de: un grand plan becomes de grand plan.

body.fr: Mais 17 % des {{jeunes|young people}} n'ont pas de {{travail|work, a job}}.

bd.meaning: But 17% of young people don't have a job.
bd.key: Negation sandwich: n'ont pas de travail — ne … pas wraps ont, then de.

body.fr: En septembre, il {{a aidé|helped}} les familles à payer les {{intérêts|interest}} de leurs prêts immobiliers.

bd.meaning: In September, it helped families pay the interest on their mortgages.
chunks: families to pay (aider quelqu'un à + plain verb)
les intérêts de leurs prêts immobiliers
bd.key: aider … à + plain verb = “help … to do”: aider les familles à payer.

body.fr: Mais l'{{effet|effect}} va être {{limité|limited}}.

bd.meaning: But the effect will be limited.
chunks: is going to be limited (aller + être)
bd.key: Future = aller + plain verb, even with être: va être = “is going to be.”

body.fr: Pour Robin Xing, la grande {{question|question}} est : {{est-ce que|(question marker)}} {{Pékin|Beijing}} va aider beaucoup plus les {{consommateurs|consumers}} ?

bd.meaning: For Robin Xing, the big question is: will Beijing do much more to help consumers?
chunks: for Robin Xing / in his view
turns a statement into a yes/no question
Beijing — the capital's name standing for the government
va aider beaucoup plus les consommateurs
is going to help consumers much more
bd.key: est-ce que + normal sentence = a question. No word-order change needed: est-ce que Pékin va aider…?

body.fr: Selon Dan Wang, d'Eurasia Group, il est {{difficile|hard}} de {{trouver du travail|find work}}.

bd.meaning: According to Dan Wang of Eurasia Group, it's hard to find work.
chunks: it is hard to (il here = 'it', no real subject)
bd.key: il est + adjective + de + plain verb = “it is ___ to …”: il est difficile de trouver.

body.fr: Alors les gens {{ont moins envie|feel less like, want less}} d'{{emprunter|borrow}}.

bd.meaning: So people are less keen to borrow.
chunks: feel less like / want less to (avoir envie de = to feel like)
bd.key: avoir envie de + plain verb = “to feel like doing”: a very common everyday way to say “want.”

grammar.fr: C'est le rythme le plus rapide
grammar.en: le plus + adjective = the superlative (“the fastest”). The adjective stays after the noun, with its own le: le rythme le plus rapide.
avoir + past participle = the past (passé composé). ont baissé, ont augmenté, a aidé. Your “past = avoir/être + verb” key.
ne … jamais = never. It works exactly like the ne … pas sandwich, and in the past it wraps the helper a, not baissé.

quiz.q: Pourquoi est-ce que les familles chinoises dépensent moins ?
quiz.a: Parce qu'elles utilisent leur argent pour rembourser leurs dettes. (Because they use their money to pay back their debts.)

flag: Compressed: I left out the bank-wide credit figures (new loans turning negative, total social financing), total household debt including business loans, and the analyst Rafael Halpin, who argues saving is bad for the economy. “The first drop” is last year's full-year fall, the first in records starting in 2005. Sales growth (0.4% vs 3.8%) is yearly growth measured each month, simplified to “on average.” “17% of young people have no job” is the youth unemployment rate, i.e. 17% of young job-seekers, not of all young people. Phrasing a native might change: attendent pour acheter is plain but a writer would more likely say remettent leurs achats à plus tard; il est difficile de trouver du travail slightly sharpens Dan Wang's “weak job prospects.” Remember: milliard = billion.
